svg.title: Credentials by workload, today
svg.desc: A matrix of the platform's credentials against its workloads: smarter-api, smarter-worker, smarter-worker-infrastructure, smarter-beat, smarter-worker-tools, the init Job, the migrate Job, the MariaDB backup CronJob and the bastion. A blue dot means the workload's code uses the credential; an orange dot means it holds the credential only because a startup check requires it; a red ring means it holds the credential and its code never uses it; a dash means it doesn't hold it. The LLM providers' and services' api keys are used only by the init Job, which copies them into Smarter Secrets; every other process reads them from the database, decrypted with the Fernet key. The MariaDB root password is used only by the init Job and the bastion, and the administrator's password only by the init Job. Every process with a database holds DJANGO_SECRET_KEY, because require_django_secret_key() refuses to start without it, though only the app signs anything. The app sends email, so it needs the SMTP password, and the infrastructure worker decrypts Smarter Secrets, so it needs the Fernet key. The app writes to the cluster and to EKS, so it needs the Kubernetes Role and the IAM role; the default worker holds the Role only for its startup check. The tool worker holds none of them: each tool call brings its own credential.
svg.text: every pod but the tool worker reads one Secret, secret-env.yaml, and most hold far more than their code uses
held only for a startup check
held, and never used: phase 3 removes it
